title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, funding and partnerships continue to shape the space landscape, with various nations and companies jockeying for position. Meanwhile, the specter of hypersonic delays looms large as the industry grapples with both innovation and bureaucracy.

themes.title: Funding Flows and Partnerships
themes.body: The UK and Florida's joint investment of $400,000 in space projects highlights a growing trend of regional collaborations. Meanwhile, German supplier deltaVision's €10.2 million raise suggests that European players are also keen to secure their slice of the pie.

themes.title: Defense Tech Developments
themes.body: KBR's reorganization to focus on Golden Dome work signals a strategic pivot towards defense technology amidst rising global tensions. This aligns with the recent $1.4 billion boost to space resilience in the FY27 budget, underscoring the increasing prioritization of security in space.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hurdles Persist
themes.body: The repeated delays in hypersonic glide vehicle tests indicate a worrying trend for defense initiatives that rely on rapid technological advancement. As the industry watches these setbacks, the implications for strategic capabilities remain a point of concern.

themes.title: Emerging Players and Innovations
themes.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding round at a $1.6 billion valuation reflects the growing interest in space domain awareness. Meanwhile, Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant passing its critical design review suggests that innovation continues to thrive, even amid broader industry challenges.
